newsitem.title: USA: Wheat trade likely topic at US-China trade meeting.
newsitem.headline: Wheat trade likely topic at US-China trade meeting.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Secretary Mickey Kantor said Sino-U.S. wheat trade probably would be discussed during meetings with Chinese Trade Minister Wu Yi later this week but he did not expect a resolution.
Kantor and Wu were scheduled to hold private talks as part of a two-day commission meeting on trade between the nations.
"I would expect to raise in private with Madame Wu a number of problems involving market access...including wheat," Kantor told reporters.
Kantor said he would "raise our concerns" but did not expect to settle the dispute over wheat and TCK smut fungus.

The long-running dispute has sharply reduced U.S. wheat sales to China. Agriculture Undersecretary Gene Moos said last week a solution was vital or the U.S. would lose a key market and China would lose access to a reliable supplier.
China has refused to accept wheat that contains TCK smut, a fungus, on grounds the disease might infect domestic crops.
U.S. officials say U.S. wheat poses no danger because wheat is milled and consumed far from China's wheat regions.
China has postponed technical-level talks on the wheat issue that were slated for this week.
